text: You just checked into your hotel, tired and ready to relax. Your first thought? Get online, check messages, or unwind with streaming.
You check networks and see 'Premium Hotel Wi-Fi'. The price tag makes your jaw drop; it costs far more than your home internet.
Why this outrageous cost? Pure greed? Hidden infrastructure? You might even consider finding a weaker, free signal elsewhere.
The invisible system is price discrimination. Hotels know *who* needs fast, reliable internet most — like business travelers on expense accounts.
They segment guests. A family needing multiple devices, or someone with an urgent deadline, will pay a premium. You're trapped by your necessity.
So, it's not the hotel's raw cost, but *your* situation. Next time, you'll recognize this invisible pricing system, and perhaps plan, or simply understand.
